description: TerraNova is a team of curious and ambitious innovators passionate about AI, technology, and space exploration. We aim to develop an innovative, data-driven solution to identify Earth locations that resemble lunar and Martian environments using NASA data. We welcome motivated members with skills in Python, AI/ML, GIS, Earth science, data analysis, research, and web development. Let’s collaborate and build something impactful!
summary:
**Orbitalith Explorer** is a planetary analog discovery platform designed to identify Earth locations that resemble environments on Mars and the Moon. We developed an interactive application that allows users to explore Earth sites, examine planetary reference regions, and compare their geological, terrain, and environmental characteristics.

Using available NASA datasets, curated classifications, and published reference values, the platform calculates similarity scores to rank potential Earth analog locations. Users can explore interactive maps, compare sites feature by feature, view data coverage, save research comparisons, export results, and access an evidence-based research assistant.

This project addresses the challenge of connecting Earth environments with extraterrestrial landscapes through accessible, data-driven exploration. It is important because identifying potential planetary analogs can support scientific research, mission preparation, and a better understanding of planetary environments. Orbitalith Explorer brings these comparisons together in one interactive platform while clearly distinguishing measured, approximate, and curated information.
details:
Project Details – Orbitalith Explorer

Orbitalith Explorer is an interactive planetary analog discovery platform that helps identify Earth locations with environmental and geological similarities to regions on Mars and the Moon.

How It Works

The platform allows users to explore selected Earth locations and planetary reference regions through interactive maps. Users can select a target region on Mars or the Moon, choose a comparison profile, and analyze potential Earth analogs. The system calculates similarity scores using available features such as landform type, geological classification, crater diameter, local relief, slope, surface roughness, aridity, and thermal conditions. It also displays data coverage so users can understand how much information supports each comparison.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Orbitalith Explorer makes planetary analog research more accessible by bringing geographic exploration, feature comparisons, and similarity analysis into one platform. It can help researchers, students, and space enthusiasts explore potential Earth environments that resemble extraterrestrial landscapes. It also encourages transparent, evidence-based comparisons rather than relying on visual resemblance alone.

Tools and Technologies

We developed the application using Python and Streamlit. The project incorporates NASA-related datasets and resources, including MOLA, LOLA, SRTM, Landsat, MODIS, SMAP, NASA PDS, and NASA Solar System Treks. Additional technologies include geospatial data processing, interactive mapping, data visualization, and evidence-based information retrieval.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of Orbitalith Explorer is its ability to connect Earth locations with both Martian and lunar environments through a unified comparison workflow. Features such as customizable comparison profiles, similarity rankings, interactive maps, site comparisons, downloadable research reports, and a research assistant make planetary exploration more interactive.

Factors Considered

Our team considered data availability, measurement compatibility, geographic coverage, scientific reliability, missing information, and transparency. We distinguish between pipeline-derived measurements, approximate literature values, and curated classifications. Similarity scores are presented as comparative indicators, not guarantees of mission suitability.
